related_questions.question: How is VLDL cholesterol calculated?
related_questions.snippet: There isn't a way to directly measure your VLDL level. Instead, you will most likely get a blood test to measure your triglyceride level. The lab can use your triglyceride level to estimate what your VLDL level is. Your VLDL is about one-fifth of your triglyceride level.

related_questions.question: What is the normal range for VLDL cholesterol?

text_blocks.snippet: A normal VLDL cholesterol level is below 30 mg/dL. Elevated VLDL levels, above 30 mg/dL, are associated with increased risk of heart disease and stroke.

list.title: What is VLDL?
list.snippet: VLDL stands for very low-density lipoprotein, and it's a type of cholesterol that carries triglycerides in the blood.

list.title: Why is it important?
list.snippet: High levels of VLDL, and the triglycerides it carries, can contribute to plaque buildup in arteries, increasing the risk of cardiovascular disease.

list.title: How is it measured?
list.snippet: VLDL cholesterol is not directly measured, but rather calculated based on triglyceride levels.

list.title: What can you do?
list.snippet: Lifestyle changes like losing weight, exercising, and eating a healthy diet (low in sugar and alcohol) can help lower VLDL levels. In some cases, medication may also be necessary.

list.title: What if my levels are high?
list.snippet: If your VLDL levels are above 30 mg/dL, talk to your doctor about strategies to lower them.
